text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha steps into fuel scarcity crisis and orders importation to normalise the situation within 48 hours.
- Government plans pay rise for university and polytechnic lecturers, says education minister Mohammed Liman.
- Nigerian police has dismissed 35 policemen for receiving bribes on the highway.
- Bank chief executives call for establishment of a rating agency to provide information on major fund users in the financial market.
- Violence in the northern state of Kano as youths protest over the acute shortage of fuel in oil-producing Nigeria.
- Opposition group NADECO, others hail fortitude of presidential claimant Moshood Abiola as they mark the third year of his detention.
- Eight hour rain disrupts business and movement in Lagos.
- Prominent African-Americans form a task force to press for stiffer sanctions including an oil embargo against Nigeria by the United States and other leading industrialised nations.
